Bereich-SceneDepth · MOD_PanoReg + MOD_PostDirector · SceneCap 0913 · results so far

SceneCap 0913 — a car park scanned twice, joined, meshed, made metric and rendered through vehicle lenses

One 360 walk and two GoPro walks through an underground car park, registered into one model, meshed by the Gaussian-splatting lane, given a provisional metric scale, and rendered person-free through the fisheye lenses of the vehicle sheet - with a range map for every frame. The production of the 30-s clips (the director) is running in a follower session.

Production director run finished at 18:18:45.
built 2026-09-15 18:23repo 19614a3work dir G:\0913SceneCapDepth_workrun record (flow chart, one card per block)flow-only pageresults panel (needs panel_serve.cmd on port 8766)

Abstract

The capture of 2026-09-13 consists of a 102.7-s Insta360 X6 walk (5,136 frames at 50 fps, 7,680×3,840 stitched) and two GoPro walks (5,591 + 5,394 frames). RealityScan 2.2 registered the 360 cube faces (1,093 of 1,236 faces at 2 Hz) and, in a second stage, 3,455 GoPro frames - but into a component of its own: no feature match crossed the two cameras. The two captures were joined by geometry instead: Metashape dense clouds of both components, a SIFT registration of their floor orthomaps and an ICP with scale (scale 0.6117, residual median 0.044 units), cross-checked by Metashape's own cross-set matching (scale 0.6111, camera centres within 0.117 units). The merged model holds 4,548 cameras and 2,492,211 points in the GoPro frame (up -Y).

The mesh comes from the Gaussian-splatting lane (RaDe-GS in the radegs container): 1,152 GoPro views at 1920 px, 30 000 iterations, 22,958,697 faces in the second run on Metashape-optimised poses. An eyeball check renders the mesh from the registered cameras: the relative range difference between the two meshes is 0.62 % (median), 92.1 % of the pixels agree within 5 %. Model units are arbitrary; the provisional metric gauge is the bay-separator pitch on the floor (3.80 units = 2.5 m, so 0.6579 m per unit), consistent with a clear height of 2.52 m and GoPro heights of 0.99 / 1.14 m.

PostDirector renders the 360 video through virtual vehicle fisheye lenses (KB4 from the vehicle sheet), keeps the carrier of the 360 camera out of view by a yaw plan, and casts a range map per frame from the mesh (16-bit, range × 500, cap 10 m). 7 cameras have been rendered over the whole walk (35,952 frames + range maps, median range 3.26 m). The remaining depth problems are holes of the mesh - 12.3 % of the floor inside the scan region has no mesh floor - and views towards the edge of the scanned area. Both are now avoided by planning: a depth-confidence region (scan positions + 5 m, 518 m²), a hole cost from a lattice of the mesh, and the director, which plans every 30-s window of the 50 fps material separately: 5 phases (instant sets) × 4 passes, all viewing axes of a window at least 5° apart, pitches -2.5 0.0 2.5°. The planning test allows 20 renderings per window (with 8 passes the chosen windows reached 22 / 24 / 35), 72 of 73 windows have at least 95 % good frames, and the end-to-end smoke run exported 2 × 300 frames with far and floor-leak pixels masked. The production run (4 lenses × 3 clips × 20 renderings = 72,000 frames + range maps) started at 15:53:44.

  • 14:40User's rule for the next capture run, recorded in the flow page: the surface lane runs optimise -> cull -> splat -> dense cloud. Metashape optimises the cameras of the merged model first, frames with wrong poses are dropped BEFORE anything is built from them, then the Gaussian splatting takes the GPU, and only when it finishes does Metashape build its dense cloud - the two GPU jobs are queued, not run beside each other (one 24 GB card). Today's run did the dense cloud first and the splat second; the cheap CPU work carries on in parallel either way.

  • 17:20User's plan for the metric gauge: AprilTag boards of known size filmed in the first and last ~10 s of each GoPro walk. The corners are triangulated through the registered cameras, so a length known in millimetres divides by the same length in model units, and a board at each end also tests scale drift along the walk. An 8 cm square gives roughly 1 % per edge and under 0.2 % once dozens of edges are averaged; a multi-tag board spanning 30-50 cm is several times better, because the error is the corner error over the measured length. Added to the flow as a planned branch off the metric gauge (pr_apriltag_scale.py still to be written); the bay-pitch gauge stays provisional until a tagged capture exists.
